interactions.summary: A student says pride can produce sloth by overestimating innate ability, and Jiang redirects the root category from pride to ego before making free will the real foundation of Dante's cosmology.

A student asks whether this clashes with theologians such as Anselm, and Jiang answers that Dante's radical move is to treat God's love as the gift of maximal free choice rather than predetermining necessity.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student theological question and Jiang answer.

interactions.summary: Jiang briefly marks that the course has already been running for ten days before moving back into the text.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang with a short student reply.

claims.claim: The student's account Jiang entertains says pride can generate sloth by making a person believe natural ability removes the need for effort.
Jiang says Dante would not make pride the ultimate ground of the sins; he would make ego the basis, understood as how one perceives oneself and one's agency in the universe.
For Jiang, the real purpose of Dante's cosmology is to secure maximum free will by preventing the soul from interpreting its condition as unavoidable divine determination.
Jiang says this free-will-first structure contradicts mainstream church theology and would have been revolutionary around the year 1300.
Jiang explicitly defines pure divine love as the gift of free will and free choice.

signature_moments.moment: Pride is demoted in favor of ego, and ego is immediately tied to the question of agency.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the ego that's the basis of everything
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shifts the moral discussion from one vice to the architecture of selfhood that makes vice possible.

signature_moments.moment: The whole cosmos is designed so the soul must never say, 'This is God's will; there is nothing I can do.'
signature_moments.source_phrase: never ever must you believe that this is God's will
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's clearest formulation of Dante as an anti-fatalistic poet of agency.

signature_moments.moment: Pure love is defined as God gifting free will and free choice.
signature_moments.source_phrase: pure love is to gift you free will and free choice
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is a strong Jiang formulation that links theology, anthropology, and the architecture of the poem.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The deeper basis of the sins, defined here as how one takes oneself, one's role, and one's agency.
Jiang's phrase for the governing purpose of Dante's cosmology: keeping choice maximally real at every point.
A political-sounding expansion of Dante's free-will structure that Jiang uses to describe the poem's human stakes.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-26 Jiang explicitly frames Dante's free-will cosmology as historically revolutionary for circa 1300 theology, not merely as a timeless spiritual commonplace.
